title: Prior work: four groups of methods
hints: 4 groups: assignment / route guidance / planners (deadlocks & collisions) / jam handling
Each fixes one kind of congestion locally
None avoids congestion at assignment level, whole system
Our question: a global scheduling algorithm?
en: 【依次指四张卡】 Earlier methods fall into four groups. **Order assignment** gives robots close, cheap orders. **Route guidance** makes busy roads cost more, so robots spread out. **Planners** decide which robot moves first, and avoid **deadlocks and collisions**. **Jam handling** keeps some robots idle, or sorts out robots that meet in a narrow passage. 【指底部黄框】 In all the methods we read, each one only fixes **one kind of congestion locally**. None starts from **the whole system** and weighs many factors to **avoid congestion when orders are given out**. {So we wanted to try:} is there a **global scheduling algorithm** that avoids congestion?
zh: 【依次指四张卡】前人的方法可以分成四类。**派单**给车分近的、便宜的单。**选路**让拥挤的路代价更高，把车分散开。**规划**决定哪台车先走，避免**死锁和碰撞**。**拥堵处理**让一部分车闲着，或者处理在窄道里碰上的车。【指底部黄框】在我们读到的所有方法里，每一种都只是**单独在局部优化某种拥塞**，没有一种从**整个系统**出发、同时考虑多个因素**在派单层面去避免拥塞**，所以我们想进行这个尝试，看看有没有一种**全局调度算法**去避免拥塞。

title: Why did changing routes not help?
figs: 图 4 地图压成网络（公式直接写在右边文字里）
hints: Model: 16 rooms = nodes, 31 doors = edges; door 6 is a cut
906 ÷ 3,614 ≈ 0.2507 (counted on the map)
14 of 15 rerouting methods lowered results → the question is scheduling
en: {So why did changing routes not help? After a week of analysis, we found the problem could be solved with a model.} 【指左图】 The **16 rooms are nodes** and the **31 doors are edges**; 【指红线门 6】 **door 6 is a cut**{: without it, the four lower-left rooms are cut off}. 【指右 1】 the lower-left rooms hold **906 of the 3,614** room cells: **906 ÷ 3,614 ≈ 0.2507**{, a quarter}. 【指右 2】 {With random pickups and deliveries,} an order must cross this narrow door 6 when its two ends are on different sides: probability **2** possible orders **× 0.2507** lower-left **× 0.7493** the rest **≈ 37.6 percent**. {That is why} **14 of 15** rerouting methods we tried lowered results. {The real question is} **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**: **scheduling**.
zh: 那为什么改路线没有用？我们经过一周的分析以后发现这个问题可以通过建模型解决。【指左图】**16 个房间是点，31 道门是线**；【指红线门 6】**门 6 是一个割**：没有它，左下 4 个房间就断开了。【指右 1】左下房间占 3614 个房间格里的 **906 个**，**906 ÷ 3614 ≈ 0.2507**，约四分之一。【指右 2】取货点和送货点随机落下时，一单两头在门的两侧才要过这个窄门 6，概率是 **2**（两种先后）**× 0.2507**（左下）**× 0.7493**（其余）**≈ 37.6%**。所以我们试过的 15 种换路办法里有 **14 种**都变差。真正的问题是**派多少车、哪边先走**，也就是**调度**。

segs.en: {So why did changing routes not help? After a week of analysis, we found the problem could be solved with a model.} 【指左图】 The **16 rooms are nodes** and the **31 doors are edges**; 【指红线门 6】 **door 6 is a cut**{: without it, the four lower-left rooms are cut off}.
segs.zh: 那为什么改路线没有用？我们经过一周的分析以后发现这个问题可以通过建模型解决。【指左图】**16 个房间是点，31 道门是线**；【指红线门 6】**门 6 是一个割**：没有它，左下 4 个房间就断开了。

segs.en: 【指右 1】 the lower-left rooms hold **906 of the 3,614** room cells: **906 ÷ 3,614 ≈ 0.2507**{, a quarter}.
segs.key: Lower-left share = lower-left room cells **906** ÷ all room cells **3,614** ≈ **0.2507**

segs.en: 【指右 2】 {With random pickups and deliveries,} an order must cross this narrow door 6 when its two ends are on different sides: probability **2** possible orders **× 0.2507** lower-left **× 0.7493** the rest **≈ 37.6 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指右 2】取货点和送货点随机落下时，一单两头在门的两侧才要过这个窄门 6，概率是 **2**（两种先后）**× 0.2507**（左下）**× 0.7493**（其余）**≈ 37.6%**。

segs.en: {That is why} **14 of 15** rerouting methods we tried lowered results. {The real question is} **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**: **scheduling**.

title: What makes our robots different
figs: 对比表（我们的车 / 计算机网络 / 道路交通，幻灯片上直接画的，阴影 = 和我们的车不一样）

→ copy neither: we had to build our own new algorithm, DoorFlow
DoorFlow never drops a robot; decides who goes and when; keeps exits clear
en: 【指表格】 Our analysis also showed where we differ from **computer networks** and **road traffic**. A congested network can simply **drop packets**; a robot **cannot be dropped**, and a waiting robot **takes up a cell**. Road traffic cannot leave some cars **standing still forever**, but here we can. And **one program decides every order and move**, not each driver. {So} we **cannot simply copy** network or traffic algorithms; we had to come up with **a completely new algorithm of our own**. Robots also **break down at random**, and once a door is jammed, scheduling can hardly cope with those breakdowns. {So} from the start we aimed to **keep exits clear**.
zh: 【指表格】同时我们的分析发现了我们和计算机网络和交通流算法不一样的地方：计算机网络里拥塞往往可以直接**丢包**来解决，车**不能因为拥塞被丢弃**；而且等着的车**占着格子**；对于交通来说，交通不能让某些车辆**永远不动**，但是这里我们可以；而且这里**每一单、每一步都由一个程序统一决定**，不像路上每个司机自己选路。所以都**不能直接抄**和借用交通流和计算机网络的算法，我们必须想出**自己全新的算法**。因为车会**随机故障**，门前出现拥堵以后，调度算法非常难处理这种随机故障，所以我们一开始的方向瞄向了**让出口保持畅通**。

title: Scheduling 1: a quota for each door
figs: 名额大小原理图（从“路上的车数 = 过门速率 × 路程时间”推出；这条计数规律在排队论里叫 Little 定律，讲稿不提名字，只写在图注里；理论示意）
hints: Robots on the way to a door: hold an order through it, not crossed yet (counted live)
Door quota = the most robots allowed on the way at once → how many orders through the door at the same time
Quota full → the next robot gets an order that does not need the door
Door takes one robot every r ticks, trip T ticks → T ÷ r on the way → quota = door rate × trip time
Metro: a train every 2 min, trip 20 min → 20 ÷ 2 = 10 trains running at once
Fewer: door waits; more: queue, block the other side

segs.en: {So how do we keep a door from jamming? Step by step. How many robots should head for a narrow door at once?} We came up with a way to **measure how many robots are on the way** to a door: robots that hold an order through it but have not crossed yet. We put a limit on this number, the **door quota**: it decides **how many orders may cross the door at the same time**.
segs.zh: 那如何避免一个门拥塞？我们一步步分析。同时该有多少车奔向窄门？我们想到一个办法：**衡量在途、会通过某个门口的车有多少**，也就是接了要过这道门的单、还没过门的车。我们给这个数设一个上限，叫**门的名额**，用它来决定**同时指派多少个要穿过这道门的任务**。
key: **Robots on the way** to a door: hold an order through it, not crossed yet (**counted live**)
**Door quota**: the most robots allowed on the way at once → **how many orders through the door at the same time**

segs.en: When a door's quota is full, the next robot gets **an order that does not need the door**.
segs.zh: 某道门的名额满了，下一台车就派**一单不用过这道门的**。
segs.key: Quota full → the next robot gets **an order that does not need the door**

segs.en: {How big should the quota be?} If the door takes one robot every **r** ticks and a trip takes **T** ticks, keeping the door busy needs everything sent in the last T ticks on the way: **T ÷ r** robots. {So} **quota = door rate × trip time**.
segs.zh: 名额该多大？如果门每 **r** 拍放进一台，一趟路要 **T** 拍，要让门一直有车过，过去 T 拍里派出的车都得在路上，也就是 **T ÷ r** 台。所以**名额 = 过门速率 × 路程时间**。
key: How big? Door passes one robot every **r** ticks · a trip takes **T** ticks
Robots on the way so the door never waits = trip time **T ÷ r** ticks per robot
**Quota = door rate × trip time**

segs.en: {An everyday example:} a metro line sends a train every **2 minutes**, and a trip takes **20 minutes**, so **20 ÷ 2 = 10 trains** are running on the line at once.
segs.zh: 生活比方：地铁每 **2 分钟**发一班，一趟全程 **20 分钟**。线路上同时跑着的车就是 **20 ÷ 2 = 10 列**。
segs.key: Everyday example: metro, a train every **2 min**, a trip **20 min** → trip **20 min ÷ 2 min** per train = **10 trains** on the line at once

segs.en: 【指左图上半】 Fewer robots, and the door **waits**; 【指左图下半】 more, and the extras only **queue** and **block the other side**.
segs.zh: 【指左图上半】车少了，门就**等车**；【指左图下半】车多了，多出来的只会**排队**，还会**挡住对面**。
segs.key: Fewer → the door **waits** · more → extras **queue** and **block the other side**

title: Why only about 26 robots per 500 ticks at door 6?

segs.en: 【指图】 {Next, we analysed the case} without jams: door 6 passes about **26 robots** per 500 ticks. {Why?} We timed **669 crossings**: one robot takes **18.7 ticks** on average: **9.2** to step up, turn and enter, about **3 moves × 3 ticks**; **4.8** for breakdowns; **2.2** for switching sides; **2.5** waiting; so **500 ticks ÷ 18.7 ticks per robot ≈ 26.7**. {Counting crossings in 5 runs agrees:} **1,175 crossings ÷ 45 periods ≈ 26**. {So} the map can finish at most door rate **26 ÷ crossing share 0.376 ≈ 69 orders** per 500 ticks, **whatever the routes**.
segs.zh: 【指图】然后我们继续分析，在没有拥塞的情况下，门 6 每 500 拍大约过 **26 台**。为什么？我们给 **669 次过门**计时，平均每过一台要 **18.7 拍**：走到门前、转身、进门 **9.2 拍**（约 **3 步 × 每步 3 拍**）；故障 **4.8 拍**；换方向 **2.2 拍**；等出口等 **2.5 拍**；所以 **500 拍 ÷ 每台 18.7 拍 ≈ 26.7 台**。在 5 局仿真里数过门的车也一样：**1175 次过门 ÷ 45 段 ≈ 26**。所以**不管车怎么走**，整张图每 500 拍最多完成 **过门速率 26 ÷ 过门比例 0.376 ≈ 69 单**。

Door rate = **500 ticks ÷ 18.7 ticks per robot ≈ 26.7 ≈ 26** robots per 500 ticks · counted in 5 runs: **1,175 crossings ÷ 45 periods ≈ 26**

title: Scheduling 2: when should the door switch sides?
figs: 门速度曲线（演讲专用：U(n) = nh / ((n−1)h + s)，h = 10、s = 34 用 5 局实测的中位数）；试过的换向规则对比表（幻灯片上直接画的）
hints: Tried: fixed timetable −5.0%, −6.4%; ≤ 80 steps per turn −1.1%; until empty = best
Same direction ≈ 10 ticks, after a switch ≈ 34 → 34 − 10 = 24 extra per switch
Timing histograms: backup slide 1

segs.en: {We tried three rules:} a **fixed timetable** lost **5.0 and 6.4 percent**; **at most 80 steps** per turn lost **1.1 percent**; **serving one side until it is empty** was best.
segs.zh: 我们试了三种规则：**按固定时间表**换，少了 **5.0% 和 6.4%**；**每轮最多放 80 步**，少了 **1.1%**；**一边走空再换**最好。
segs.key: Tried **three switching rules** (table)

segs.en: {Why?} A switch costs much more than one more robot: the first robot after a switch needs about **34 ticks**, the next one in the same direction only **10**. {So} serving one side until it is empty is best.
segs.zh: 为什么？换一次方向比多放一台车贵得多：换向后第一台要隔大约 **34 拍**，同方向下一台只要 **10 拍**。所以一边走空再换最好。
segs.key: A switch costs far more: after a switch **34 ticks**, same direction only **10** → **serve until empty**

segs.en: 【指公式】 A turn of **n** robots takes **34** for the first + **10 × (n − 1)** for the rest, instead of **10 × n**. 【指曲线左端】 One robot per turn: needs **10**, takes **34**, **10 ÷ 34 = 29 percent** of top speed; 【指 n = 10】 ten per turn: needs **100**, takes **34 + 90**, **100 ÷ 124 = 81 percent**.
key: Turn of **n**: first **34** + rest **10 × (n − 1)** ticks, instead of **10 × n**
Door speed = needed ÷ taken: 1 per turn **10 ÷ 34 = 29%** · 10 per turn **100 ÷ (34 + 90) = 81%** → serve **until empty**

en: {We tried three rules:} a **fixed timetable** lost **5.0 and 6.4 percent**; **at most 80 steps** per turn lost **1.1 percent**; **serving one side until it is empty** was best. {Why?} A switch costs much more than one more robot: the first robot after a switch needs about **34 ticks**, the next one in the same direction only **10**. {So} serving one side until it is empty is best. 【指公式】 A turn of **n** robots takes **34** for the first + **10 × (n − 1)** for the rest, instead of **10 × n**. 【指曲线左端】 One robot per turn: needs **10**, takes **34**, **10 ÷ 34 = 29 percent** of top speed; 【指 n = 10】 ten per turn: needs **100**, takes **34 + 90**, **100 ÷ 124 = 81 percent**.
zh: 我们试了三种规则：**按固定时间表**换，少了 **5.0% 和 6.4%**；**每轮最多放 80 步**，少了 **1.1%**；**一边走空再换**最好。为什么？换一次方向比多放一台车贵得多：换向后第一台要隔大约 **34 拍**，同方向下一台只要 **10 拍**。所以一边走空再换最好。【指公式】一轮放 **n** 台要 **第一台 34 + 其余 10 × (n − 1)** 拍，而不换向只要 **10 × n** 拍。【指曲线左端】每轮 1 台：本来要 **10**，实际 **34**，**10 ÷ 34 = 29%**；【指 n = 10】每轮 10 台：本来要 **100**，实际 **34 + 90**，**100 ÷ 124 = 81%**。

en: {To conclude.} 【指 1】 **DoorFlow does not make each robot smarter**; it controls **how many robots head for a door, and which side goes first**. 【指 2】 Changing routes did not help, but **scheduling** did: on the official room map, **140.5 percent** more orders than the official starter program. 【指 3】 For a real warehouse, this means **a quota for each direction when orders are given out, and one direction at a time in narrow aisles**. Thank you. We are happy to take your questions.

title: Backup 1: how long does the door take?
figs: 门 6 过门间隔的实测（演讲专用：5 局仿真，官方房间图 250 台，DoorFlow，1255 次过门；figures/deck/demo/door_timing.py）
hints: 5 runs (seeds 9700–9704), official map, 250 robots, DoorFlow: 1,255 crossings of door 6 timed
Same direction: mostly 6 or 9 ticks = 2 or 3 moves (3 ticks per move); median 10
Switch: median 34 ticks (door + 4-cell buffer must empty) → 34 − 10 = 24 extra per switch

segs.en: We ran **5 simulations** and timed all **1,255 crossings** of door 6.
segs.zh: 我们跑了 **5 局仿真**，记下门 6 全部 **1255 次过门**的时间。

segs.en: 【指左图】 Same direction: the next robot usually comes **6 or 9 ticks** later, **2 or 3 moves**, as the competition sets **3 ticks** per move; median **10 ticks**.
segs.zh: 【指左图】同一个方向：下一台车通常隔 **6 拍或 9 拍**，也就是 **2 步或 3 步**，因为比赛设定走一步要 **3 拍**；中位数 **10 拍**。

segs.en: 【指右图】 After a switch, the first robot comes a median of **34 ticks** later: the door and the 4-cell buffer must empty first. {So} each switch costs about **34 − 10 = 24 extra ticks**.
segs.zh: 【指右图】换方向后，第一台车的中位数要隔 **34 拍**：门和 4 格缓冲区要先清空。所以每换一次方向，大约多花 **34 − 10 = 24 拍**。
segs.key: Extra per switch = switch gap **34** − normal gap **10** = **24 ticks**
